items.definition: The people who watch or listen to a performance, film or talk.
examples: The audience stood up and applauded for nearly five minutes.
The play is aimed at a young audience.

items.definition: A public display of paintings, photographs or other objects, usually in a gallery or museum.
examples: We went to an exhibition of early photography at the weekend.
The exhibition runs until the end of March.

items.definition: A place where an event such as a concert, match or conference takes place.
examples: The old cinema has been turned into a music venue.
Tickets are cheap, but the venue is a long way from the centre.

items.definition: A live concert given by a band or a musician, especially a small one.
examples: My cousin's band is playing a gig in Leeds on Saturday.
It was the best gig I've been to all year.

items.definition: To practise a play, a piece of music or a speech so that you are ready to perform it in front of other people.
examples: The actors have been rehearsing the final scene all week.
She rehearsed her speech in front of the mirror.

items.definition: The buildings, traditions and customs that a country or community has had for a long time and that are considered important.
examples: The town is proud of its industrial heritage.
Many old churches are protected as part of the national heritage.

items.definition: An extremely good painting, book, film or piece of music, often the best work of an artist.
examples: Many critics regard the film as a masterpiece.
The gallery owns several masterpieces from the seventeenth century.

items.definition: Used when all the tickets for an event have been bought, so no more are available.
examples: I tried to get tickets, but the show was sold out in ten minutes.
The tour has sold out in every city.

items.definition: To relax and stop feeling tense or worried after a period of work or stress.
examples: I like to unwind with a book after a busy day.
A long walk by the river is the best way to unwind.

items.definition: To start doing an activity or hobby regularly.
examples: After he retired, he took up painting.
I'd like to take up a new sport this autumn.

items.definition: Something you do regularly for pleasure in your free time.
examples: Fishing is his favourite pastime.
Reading used to be the national pastime on long train journeys.

items.definition: All the actors who perform in a play, film or television series.
examples: The cast spent three months rehearsing before the opening night.
It's a great film, but the supporting cast is even better.

items.definition: To want to do or have something; to feel like doing something.
examples: Do you fancy going to the cinema tonight?
I don't fancy a long walk in this weather.

items.definition: To like something a lot or to be very interested in an activity.
examples: My sister is very keen on contemporary dance.
I'm not that keen on musicals, to be honest.

items.definition: A person whose job is to give opinions on books, films, plays or music, usually in a newspaper or online.
examples: The film critic gave the new thriller only two stars.
Critics praised the exhibition but complained about the ticket prices.

items.definition: Something very impressive or unusual to look at, such as a large public event or a dramatic scene.
examples: The fireworks over the harbour were an unforgettable spectacle.
The opening ceremony was a huge spectacle of light and music.

trap.en: A theatre or circus performance is a show, not a spectacle. A spectacle is something striking to look at, and make a spectacle of yourself means to behave in an embarrassing way in public.
trap.es: Un espectáculo de teatro o de circo es a show. Spectacle es algo muy llamativo de ver; make a spectacle of yourself es hacer el ridículo en público.
